passed_story_test.044: Chandra's curse by Daksha, Shiva wears him (Shiva Purana / Somnath legend)
passed_story_test.045: Shankhachuda, conch and tulsi not offered to Shiva (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Yuddha Khanda)
passed_story_test.046: Parashurama breaks Ganesha's tusk (Brahmanda / Brahmavaivarta Puranas)
passed_story_test.047: Raksha mantra names Bali (Bhagavata 8.18-22; mantra tradition)
passed_story_test.049: Jagannath idols unfinished (Skanda Purana Utkala Khanda; Orissa Review)
passed_story_test.050: Shrivatsa and Bhrigu (Bhagavata 10.89; Vaishnava tradition, told with कहते हैं)
passed_story_test.051: Coconut as Trishanku's head (Ramayana for Trishanku; coconut link is folk, told as लोक-कथा)
passed_story_test.052: Murugan peacock and rooster (Kanda Puranam, Tamil tradition)
passed_story_test.053: Water on Shivling after Halahala (Bhagavata 8.7; the cooling link is tradition)
passed_story_test.054: Mushak is Krauncha (Ganesha Purana, told with कहते हैं)
passed_story_test.055: Rudraksha from Shiva's tears (Devi Bhagavata / Shiva Purana; chapter not verified)
passed_story_test.056: Hanuman and sindoor (folk tradition, stated as such; no text named)
passed_story_test.057: Garuda as Vishnu's vahana (Mahabharata Adi Parva 29-33)
passed_story_test.058: Damaru and the Maheshvara Sutras (Nandikeshvara Kashika; tradition)
passed_story_test.059: Durva and Analasura (popular tradition, no text named)
passed_story_test.060: Sudarshana chakra from Shiva (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
passed_story_test.061: Durga's weapons from the gods (Devi Mahatmya ch. 2)
passed_story_test.063: Tulsi and Shaligram (Brahmavaivarta Purana tradition; kept consistent with 045)
passed_story_test.064: Ganesha and Tulsi curse each other (Brahmavaivarta Purana, Ganesha Khanda; told with कहते हैं)

rejected.मंदिर में घंटी क्यों: no story and no scriptural source found, only modern explanations
rejected.परिक्रमा दाएँ से क्यों: no story source; the Ganesha-parikrama tale is too well known and does not explain the direction
rejected.माला में 108 दाने: a number with competing explanations, no story
rejected.लक्ष्मी का वाहन उल्लू: only folk versions, one makes Indra the owl, which is disrespectful to a deity
rejected.विष्णु का शेषनाग पर सोना: no story source found, only symbolism
rejected.कृष्ण के मुकुट पर मोरपंख: only Braj folk belief, nothing sourceable and no real payoff
rejected.काली की जीभ बाहर क्यों: the shame story is a later popular tradition, not in the Puranas, and it could be read as insulting; competing readings
rejected.नंदी के कान में मन्नत: no source found for the practice
rejected.शनिवार पीपल की पूजा: Pippalada defeating Shani is in the Shiva Purana, but the Saturday-and-peepal link was not found in any source
rejected.एकादशी पर चावल क्यों नहीं: only blogs; the Medha story was not traced to any text (kept as a spare, not made)
rejected.शिव की तीसरी आँख: no sourced origin; only the Kamadeva burning, which is a different story
rejected.दुर्गा का शेर (as a separate reel): folded into 061, since Devi Mahatmya says Himavan gave the lion
rejected.छप्पन भोग क्यों: the 7 days x 8 meals story could not be confirmed in any source I could reach
rejected.विष्णु का पाञ्चजन्य शंख: valid (Bhagavata/Harivamsha) but overlaps 045 on conch; spare for later
rejected.कार्तिकेय के छह मुख: valid but not run yet; spare for later (series already at 12)
